chat_context:
Exceptional Solutions PT (Exceptional Solutions Physical Therapy), Grand Rapids, Michigan. A new, owner-run clinic specializing in physical therapy for chronic pain, hypermobility and Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome (EDS/hEDS).

Clinician: Samantha Newell, DPT, the owner and currently the only employee (no PTAs, never PT techs). She has Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome herself (her site says EDS and does not name the type, so never say hEDS about her) and a lifetime of personal experience with hypermobility and chronic pain. Completed the EDS ECHO training for practitioners through the Ehlers-Danlos Society. Calvin College graduate (kinesiology, psychology, French), DPT graduated 2022.

Approach: one-on-one, gentle, individualized care with no standard protocols (she does not use the Muldowney protocol). Movement re-training and muscle control first, before strengthening, to avoid pain and injury in hypermobile bodies. Combines traditional physical therapy with somatic and nervous system re-education and holistic methods. Trauma-informed and neurodivergent-friendly. Listens to the patient's story and believes them. Great fit for people whose past physical therapy didn't help or made things worse.

Conditions: chronic pain (pain lasting 3+ months), hypermobility, Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome, joint pain and instability, pre- and post-op care, chronic back pain. Also sees kids and teens with joint pain. Takes out-of-state patients (the clinic is about 10 minutes from motels and restaurants).

Insurance accepted: BCBS (Blue Cross Blue Shield), Medicare Plus Blue, BCN (Blue Care Network), BCNA (Blue Care Network Advantage), Original Medicare, Tricare East, Original Medicaid, PPO ASR/HAP plans. Recently accepted: Priority Health and Aetna. Still in process: Humana, Molina, United, Cigna. Original Medicare allows a full hour of treatment. Medicare Advantage plans require more documentation to keep care authorized. Works with health sharing plans like CHM until reimbursement arrives. Superbills available for out-of-network benefits. Referrals are not required, but insurance requires a prescription before it pays.

Grand opening special (cash pay, for patients whose insurance is still being credentialed): up to a 1.5 hour initial evaluation for $90, and follow-ups for $45 per half hour.

Cash-pay wellness pricing: 30 min wellness treatment $60, 60 min $120, 90 min wellness evaluation $180. Standard Wellness Package (8 half-hour sessions) $400. Premium Wellness Package (12 half-hour sessions) $575. Silver Holistic Package (90 min evaluation + 8 one-hour treatments) $910. Gold Holistic Package (90 min evaluation + 12 one-hour treatments) $1,225. Workout plan at your gym $150. Keep It Going Package (12 monthly half-hour follow-ups + two workout plans) $900.

First step: a free consultation, a Google Meet video call with Samantha to talk through what's going on and whether her approach is a fit. This is what you book. The initial evaluation (billed to insurance, or the $90 grand opening evaluation if their insurance is still in process) comes after.

Location: 1444 Michigan Ave, Suite 2, Grand Rapids, MI 49503 (between Fuller and Plymouth, minutes off I-196 at the Fuller exit, near the Medical Mile). Parking and entrance are behind the building; Suite 2 is the first door on the left. Hours: by appointment only, with early mornings, evenings and weekends available. Contact: call or text (616) 430-8172, SNewell@ExceptionalSolutionsPT.net.

Real patient review (Julia): she came in exhausted from joint pain, and Samantha was the first medical professional who truly understood what she was going through.

math.label: The math
math.headline: What Foundations is *worth* to a one-person clinic
math.intro: Estimated monthly impact for a clinic your size. Each number shows how it was worked out: published research for the rates, and your own prices for the dollar values.

stats.label: Leads contacted within an hour were 7 times as likely to qualify as leads contacted even an hour later.
stats.source: Harvard Business Review · Oldroyd et al. 2011 · 1.25M leads

stats.label: fewer missed appointments with text reminders: attendance rose from 67.8% to 78.6%.
mean no-show rate across US outpatient PT clinics
stats.source: Bokinskie et al. 2015 · national survey, 634 clinics

math.note: These are estimates, not a promise. Actual results depend on your inquiry volume, your prices and how many people book.

outcomes.s: a month you're not texting back, answering questions and scheduling
outcomes.how: We assume about **30 inquiries a month** for a solo practice (texts, calls, website and Facebook messages), each taking about **15 minutes** to answer and schedule. 30 × 15 minutes = **7.5 hours** the agent handles instead of you, worth about $900 at your $120 hourly rate.

outcomes.s: a month, from about 2 extra patients and fewer no-shows
outcomes.how: Replying within minutes matters: leads contacted within an hour are **7x as likely** to turn into real prospects (Harvard Business Review). We assume that, plus follow-up and reactivation, books **2 extra patients a month**. 2 × $910 (your Silver Holistic package) = $1,820, plus 2.6 saved visits × $60 = **$158**.

outcomes.s: of missed visits prevented by automatic text reminders
outcomes.how: In a Cochrane review of 7 trials (5,841 people), text reminders raised attendance from **67.8% to 78.6%**, about a third fewer missed visits. A national survey of 634 US outpatient PT clinics found a **10.4%** average no-show rate, so on 80 visits a month that's about 8 missed visits, and **2.6** saved.

outcomes.s: and it pays for itself with a single new patient
outcomes.how: **$1,980** estimated added revenue ÷ **$500** a month ≈ 4x. One new patient on your $910 package already covers Foundations, before counting the 7.5 hours you get back.
